bull.b: Long-duration NBMs materially improve revenue visibility and deepen strategic ties with Datacenter and Edge customers. Their growing share of bits can reduce reliance on transactional sales, support planning and investment, and create a more durable foundation for future cash generation.

The shift toward datacenter and AI-related storage places SanDisk in faster-growing, higher-value applications than traditional removable media. Continued BiCS and high-bandwidth flash development can strengthen product competitiveness, improve mix, and support sustained demand over multiple quarters.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and balance sheet
bull.b: Robust cash conversion and very low leverage give SanDisk substantial financial flexibility during a cyclical recovery. A stronger balance sheet can fund technology transitions, capacity needs and shareholder returns while reducing solvency and refinancing pressure if industry conditions weaken.

bear.b: The sharp reversal demonstrates that profitability remains highly dependent on NAND market conditions and pricing cycles. Prior losses and volatile margins make current earnings power less predictable, so sustaining the 2026 step-change is essential for durable returns and investment capacity.

Demand exceeding supply supports pricing but also limits SanDisk’s ability to serve incremental customers and fully capture market growth. Higher inventory requirements further temper sellable bits, tying near-term execution and revenue realization to capacity and working-capital management.

NBMs improve visibility but also concentrate revenue and bargaining exposure among fewer major customers. Dependence on large strategic partners could amplify the impact of delayed deployments, changing requirements or contract execution issues despite the stated financial guarantees.
